questions.question_text: Apart from hallucinogens the drug capable of producing bad trips and persistent �ashbacks is
questions.explanation:
A bad trip is the most common adverse e�ect of LSD and related substances. It resembles the acute panic reaction but sometimes can be
more severe and occasionally associated with psychotic symptoms. A bad trip ends when the immediate e�ects of the hallucinogen wear o�
though its course is variable. Cannabis can also cause a bad trip.

questions.question_text: Anandamide receptors are associated with
questions.explanation:
Cannabis is the most commonly used illegal drug, with only a small minority of cannabis users ever using any other illegal drug. It is available
in various forms that contain at least 60 psychoactive cannabinoids, the most important of which is 9-delta-tetrahydrocannibinol (THC).
Cannabis usage can vary from infrequent situational use to heavy daily use. There are speci�c cannabinoid receptors in the human brain,
and the endogenous agonist at this receptor is called anandamide. The role of the endocannabinoid system is yet to be de�ned.
Anandamide (weak ligand) are formed from arachidonic acid - belong to endocannabinoid family. The two types of cannabinoid receptors,
central (CB1) and peripheral (CB2), bind tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the active ingredient of marijuana. Anandamide lowers intraocular
pressure, decreases activity level, and relieves pain. Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 546

questions.question_text: According to the modi�cations of 1971 Misuse of Drugs Act in the UK, which of the following was brie�y classi�ed as a class C drug?
questions.explanation:
Class A drugs- Include: Ecstasy, LSD, heroin, cocaine, crack, magic mushrooms (whether prepared or fresh), methyl amphetamine (crystal
meth), other amphetamines if prepared for injection Class B drugs- Amphetamines, Methylphenidate (Ritalin), Pholcodine Class C drugs-
Tranquilisers (including benzodiazepines, z-drugs and gabapen�noids), khat, some painkillers, GHB (Gamma-hydroxybutyrate). 
Ketamine was originally in class C but was upgraded to class B in 2014. 
Cannabis was originally in class B but was downgraded brie�y to class C between 2004 and 2009.

questions.question_text:
Mr. X was taken to A&E department following ingestion of a street drug and complained of a sensation of bugs crawling beneath the skin.
This could be caused by intoxication with
questions.explanation:
Cocaine Intoxication: There is increased energy, increased con�dence, heightened self-esteem, and perceived improvement on mental and
physical tasks, euphoria, and diminished need for sleep. With high doses agitation, irritability, impaired judgment, impulsive aggression,
some symptoms of mania with associated tachycardia, hypertension, and mydriasis are noted. In some, a sensation of bugs crawling
beneath the skin (formication) has been reported when under the in�uence.

questions.question_text: A patient presents with amphetamine withdrawal at A&E. Which of the following features is most likely to be present?
questions.explanation:
Amphetamine is a stimulant that acts by increasing catecholamine availability at synapses. So intoxication must cause symptoms of
sympathetic stimulation such as agitation, high blood pressure, palpitations, dry mouth, diarrhoea, di�cult micturition, increased sweating,
and mydriasis (dilated pupils) In some cases intense paranoid thoughts, hypomania and psychotic features can occur. If withdrawal takes
place, the symptoms are those of sympathetic underactivity. Chronic use may lead to loss of appetite and weight loss (hence its abuse by
those who want to stay slim!). During amphetamine withdrawal, a 'crash'occurs with anxiety, shakiness, unpleasant mood, fatigue,
nightmares with rebound REM sleep, headache, profuse sweating (also seen in intoxication), and insatiable hunger (loss of anorexic e�ect).
These symptoms peak in 48 to 96 hours and are resolved in 1 week. Kaplan and Sadock. Synopsis of Psychiatry 9th ed. Page 410

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a feature of Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
The classical triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion is rarely present in Wernicke's encephalopathy. The syndrome is much more
common than is widely believed. A presumptive diagnosis of Wernicke's encephalopathy should, therefore, be made in any patient
undergoing detoxi�cation who experiences any of the following signs; Ataxia, Hypothermia and hypotension, Confusion, ophthalmoplegia/
Nystagmus, Memory disturbance and coma/unconsciousness.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is reported as an acute adverse e�ect of MDMA use?
questions.explanation:
Acute harmful e�ects of MDMA include "increased sweating, nausea and vomiting, and diminished potency despite increased libido. Deaths
have occurred associated with dehydration and hyperthermia (a toxic reaction similar to serotonin syndrome appears to exist. Chronic
harmful e�ects include possible neuro-toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and possible chronic cognitive impairment. There is tolerance to its e�ects,
but dependence does not occur. Hangover e�ects develop 24-48 hours after ingestion including fatigue, anorexia, and depressed mood
(which may be severe)". Excerpt from Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry; 2e:543

questions.question_text:
A 12-year-old boy presents with dizziness, tremors and nystagmus. The urine drug test is negative for alcohol, opioids and amphetamines.
Which of the following drugs must be suspected?
questions.explanation:
Inhalants are often used by adolescents. No dependence syndrome described with inhalants; no withdrawals noted as per DSM.Signs of
intoxication include "dizziness, nystagmus, incoordination, slurred speech, unsteady gait, lethargy, depressed re�exes, psychomotor
retardation, tremor, generalized muscle weakness, blurred vision or diplopia, stupor or coma and euphoria". A recent inhalant user may
have rashes around nose and mouth; unusual breath odours; the residue of the inhalant substances on body or clothes; and signs of ocular
and oropharyngeal irritation. Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is least likely in those with MDMA withdrawal?
questions.explanation:
MDMA abstinence-associated withdrawal symptoms include fatigue, loss of appetite, depression, anxiety, and trouble concentrating. This
happens on the same day or 2days after drug use, the most common mental or mood complaints are di�culty concentrating, depression,
anxiety and fatigue. These symptoms strongly resemble a miniature "crash" that is seen as a withdrawal reaction after the use of stimulants.
Insomnia (a delay or postponement of sleep) may be seen during active use or intoxication.

questions.question_text: A frequent feature of benzodiazepine withdrawal among the following is
questions.explanation: Insomnia is the most frequent feature of BDZ withdrawal and anxiety is the most prominent.

questions.question_text:
A 34-year-old man admitted for opioid detoxi�cation has a blood pressure of 96/68 mm Hg. Which of the following is a preferred medication
for opioid detoxi�cation?
questions.explanation:
Clonidine can cause a drop in BP; though lofexidine belongs to the same class, it has less propensity for this e�ect. The best choice in this
situation is buprenorphine that is not provided in the MCQ as an option.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is a classic synthetic hallucinogen?
questions.explanation:
Classic synthetic hallucinogen LSD was �rst synthesized in 1938 by Albert Ho�man from the ergot alkaloids. The compound is also noted in
rye fungus that contributed to lethal outbreaks of St. Anthony's �re'in the Middle Ages. The compounds are also present in morning glory
seeds in low concentrations.

questions.question_text:
Mrs. X has a history of opioid dependence and is still taking it. She is pregnant now and is willing to consider opioid detoxi�cation. This
should be ideally done during
questions.explanation:
Women who are pregnant or planning a pregnancy should consider treatment with Methadone. Ideally, the mother should be encouraged
to become abstinent prior to delivery-often this may not be possible. If pregnancy begins while a woman is taking high doses of methadone,
the dosage should be reduced slowly (e.g., 1 mg every three days), and foetal monitoring must be carried out closely.If considering
detoxi�cation, this should be done in the middle trimester - avoid �rst trimester for the fear of abortion and last trimester for the fear of
premature birth.

questions.question_text: The lifetime prevalence of dysthymia is
questions.explanation: The lifetime prevalence of dysthymia is 2.5-5% worldwide (Warraich and colleagues 2004). The male: female ratio is 1:2

questions.question_text: Which of the following SSRIs has an active metabolite?
questions.explanation:
Sertraline also has an active metabolite, N-desmethyl sertraline, which is ten times less potent than sertraline itself. Fluoxetine also has an
active metabolite nor�uoxetine with a long half-life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following suggests life-threatening symptom of serotonergic syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Severe serotonin syndrome can be life-threatening. Signs and symptoms include high fever, seizures, irregular heartbeat or
unconsciousness

questions.question_text:
A 28-year-old man is taking clozapine for the last eight months but still has some interfering positive symptoms despite good concordance
and optimum plasma levels. What is the best-proven strategy to augment this treatment?
questions.explanation:
Clozapine augmentation has become common practice because an inadequate response to clozapine alone is a frequent clinical event.
Clozapine augmentation with Amisulpride has some evidence that suggests this approach may be worthwhile. It may also allow a dose
reduction in clozapine for those who have a dose-dependent intolerance. (Ref: The Maudsley prescribing guidelines in psychiatry- 11th
edition- 67)

questions.question_text:
A 33-year-old man who is taking clozapine for the last 15 days presents with unspeci�c clinical symptoms such as fever and tachycardia.
After carrying out some blood tests and reviewing the results, you are suspecting myocarditis. The next best step is to;

options.text: Monitor cardiac enzymes for next 3 days
Stop clozapine and refer to cardiology
Stop clozapine and send patient to the A&E
Start digoxin after discussing with the GP

correct_answer.text: Stop clozapine and refer to cardiology

questions.explanation:
Because in rare cases clozapine-induced myocarditis can progress rapidly into cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure, all patients
should be monitored closely for at least the initial four weeks of treatment. This should include assessment of clinical status for subjective
signs of distress, vital signs each visit, electrocardiogram at baseline, and if risks is suspected then weekly laboratory tests including 3Es:
eosinophils, ESR (or CRP) and enzymes (troponin). A diagnosis of myocarditis should be followed by prompt discontinuation of clozapine and
medical follow-up (urgently refer to a cardiologist) for supportive treatment. It is not an emergency requiring an approach to the A&E.
(Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for premature ejaculation?
questions.explanation: SSRIs can cause delayed - not premature - ejaculation.

questions.question_text:
A 33-year-old lady has repeated episodes of high mood, euphoria and spending spree followed by long periods of low mood, sleep
disturbances and suicidal ideas. What is the prevalence of her psychiatric diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The description �ts with bipolar disorder. Consistently in large epidemiological studies, 1.5% prevalence is quoted for bipolar disorders. It is
unclear if there is an elevated estimation of depressive disorders and under-diagnosis of bipolar type 2 disorder in these surveys.

questions.question_text:
A 40-year-old lady complains of a 5-year history of headache, nausea, vomiting, di�culty swallowing and unusual pains in her arms and legs.
All physical investigations have been normal, and the medical team doubt the presence of an organic pathology. Which is the most likely
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Somatization disorder is characterised by multiple, recurrent and frequently changing physical symptoms; most patients have a long and
complicated history of involvement with medical services.

questions.question_text:
A 60-year-old man presents with a persistently low mood, early morning waking and a reduced appetite. His wife reports that he has
stopped looking after himself but is still drinking adequate amounts of �uid. She thinks his current presentation is related to the death of
the family dog. On further questioning, the man reports odd beliefs and admits to hearing voices. Which of the following would you
recommend in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis is severe depression with psychotic symptoms as he has both mood and psychotic symptoms. Both antidepressants and
antipsychotics should be used in the treatment of psychotic depression as the �rst line. Emergency ECT is recommended if a patient is not
eating and drinking, which is not the case in this scenario.

questions.question_text: A patient with the bipolar disorder has become manic. What treatment would you give?
questions.explanation:
Among mood stabilisers, both Lithium and sodium valproate are recommended as the �rst line treatment of mania. If the patient is taking
any antidepressant medication, it should be stopped immediately.

questions.question_text:
What is the threshold of considering a drug teratogenic compared to the spontaneous occurrence of major malformations among live-born
neonates?
questions.explanation:
The incidence of commonly occurring and clinically identi�able abnormalities recognized at birth among liveborn infants is 2%-4% in most
series published. If exposure to a treatment is associated with a rate higher that this, the treatment can be suspected to have a teratogenic
potential.

questions.question_text: The migrants-to-natives prevalence ratio for schizophrenia is estimated to be
questions.explanation:
The incidence of schizophrenia is 3 to 5 times more common in migrants than native population; this becomes 1.8 when considering
prevalence rates.(Saha, McGrath et al PLoS Medicine 2004).

questions.question_text: Patients su�ering from schizophrenia are often seen to be living in inner cities. This is explained by
questions.explanation:
The increased frequency of schizophrenia in lower socio-economic groups, urban dwellers and immigrants may be because deprivation
causes schizophrenia – the breeder hypothesis – or because the functional decline associated with schizophrenia drives schizophrenic (and
preschizophrenic) individuals to cheaper inner city accommodation – the drifter hypothesis. The drifter hypothesis enjoys wider acceptance
and is supported by reports of high rates of schizophrenia in homeless people (Marshall, 1994) and in Afro-Caribbean immigrants to the UK.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of mania among relatives of individuals with bipolar disorder, as determined by structured clinical interviews, is
questions.explanation:
The kappa agreement between structured and clinical diagnostic techniques for mood disorders is poor, ranging from 0.23 to 0.49 in
ESEMED study. In the IOWA Study (a prospective investigation of the hereditary nature of schizophrenia and bipolar disorders) the
prevalence of mania among relatives of patients a�ected by bipolar disorders, calculated solely on the basis of diagnostic interviews, was
1.9%; however, when additional sources of information such as clinical records and cross-interviewing of relatives were considered, the rate
increased to 5.3%.

questions.question_text: The personality disorders associated with highest disability in terms of vocational functioning is
questions.explanation:
Seminal work by Skodol et al ((Am J Psychiatry 2002; 159:276-283) showed that obsessive-compulsive personality disorder was associated
with the least overall functional impairment among the personality disorders, while borderline PD and schizotypal PD had the highest
impairment in baseline occupational functioning.

questions.question_text:
A 23-year-old man �nds it hard to delegate his job to others. He is rigid and in�exible in adhering to rules and has had various altercations
with co-workers concerning his inability to get rid of old �les from his o�ce. What is the prevalence of his diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The most striking features of anankastic personality disorder are included in this description. Along with a lack of adaptability to new
situations, patients show a lack of imagination, failing to take advantage of opportunities, inhibiting perfectionism making ordinary work a
burden and harbour a guilty preoccupation with wrong doing. 17 to 19 per 1000 is the quoted prevalence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales retain the aspects of a clinical examination during a consultation?
questions.explanation: PSE retains the aspects of a mental state examination

questions.question_text: Which is NOT true regarding depression?

options.text: Ethnic minorities and migrants have consistently high rate of depression
Poverty and unemployment are associated with depression across all cultures
Cognitive schemas in depression vary across the cultures
Selective migration of vulnerable individuals cannot explain the incidence of depression among immigrants
Somatic complaints are more frequent among immigrant depressed patients

correct_answer.text: Ethnic minorities and migrants have consistently high rate of depression

questions.explanation:
Unlike psychosis, depression does not seem to be consistently high in the ethnic minorities. Dinesh Bhugra and Oyedeji Ayonrinde,
"Depression in migrants and ethnic minorities," Adv Psychiatr Treat 10, no. 1 (January 1, 2004): 13-17.

questions.question_text: Which of the following personality disorders is often included in the bipolar spectrum?
questions.explanation:
The relationship between borderline personality disorder and bipolar disorder has been a controversial topic ever since borderline
personality disorder was incorporated into DSM in 1980. Some authors argue for a shared spectrum between the two groups.

questions.question_text:
A nursing mother treated for her bipolar illness brings her 3 weeks old infant to her paediatrician. The baby is hypotonic, lethargic and not
taking feeds. On investigation, the baby has elevated liver functions indicating cholestasis. The most likely o�ending agent is
questions.explanation:
Carbamazepine is excreted via breast milk and can cause cholestatic hepatitis, transient hepatitic dysfunction (Hyperbilirubinaemia, High
concentration of gamma-glutamyl-transferase), and seizure like activity, irritability, high-pitched crying, hyperexcitablity and poor feeding in
a breast-fed baby.

questions.question_text:
A mother with bipolar disorder becomes accidentally pregnant despite using barrier contraception. The child shows developmental delays
and �ngernail hypoplasia. The most likely mood stabilizer that was prescribed to the mother is
questions.explanation:
In a series of carbamazepine exposed pregnancies, craniofacial defects (11 percent), �ngernail hypoplasia (26 percent), and developmental
delay (20 percent) were recorded. (Jones et al 1989)

questions.question_text: Which antidepressant is most e�ective in pathological emotionalism according to RCT evidence?
questions.explanation:
Pathological laughing and crying syndrome is also called as emotional incontinence/emotionalism/pseudobulbar a�ect. This refers to
spontaneous unprovoked laughter or crying seen in patients wioth brain damage; it occurs in response to non-speci�c stimuli, in the
absence of associated mood change (mood incongruent a�ect) and in the absence of voluntary control of facial expression. The a�ect
change is generally transient but distressing due to perceived loss of control. In a study 66% of people with MS and pathological laughing /
crying responded to 75 mg of amitriptyline per day. Improvement in symptoms also occur with either amantadine or levodopa
administration. Fluoxetine and sertraline have been evaluated in small parallel RCTs with favourable results; citalopram in a cross over RCT
showed signi�cant bene�ts and fewer side-e�ects, and is commonly used by clinicians.

questions.question_text: Persistent apnoea has been reported in babies with which of the following drugs started during breastfeeding?
questions.explanation:
Benzodiazepines: Should not be started during breast feeding and should be encouraged to stop before becoming pregnant. Long acting
benzodiazepine can produce lethargy, poor suckling and weight loss. Persistent apnoea has been reported with Clonazepam Low dose of
short acting benzodiazepine (Temazepam, oxazepam) are mostly safe. Diazepam and alprazolam should be avoided

questions.question_text: The most epileptogenic among the newer antipsychotics is
questions.explanation: Clozapine is very epileptogenic. Among 5% who receive more than 600 mg/day develop seizures.

questions.question_text:
Mr.X is a 37-year-old gentleman with a long-standing diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia for the last 15 years. He also has a history of
deliberate self-harm and 2 episodes of failed serious suicide attempts in the past. Which of the following medications would be more
e�ective in reducing suicidal behaviour in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Clozapine reduces suicide rate in patients with schizophrenia. The Intercept Study compared Clozapine and Olanzapine in 980 patients over
a 2 year period and found that the Clozapine group had substantially fewer suicide attempts and fewer hospitalisations related to suicidality.

questions.question_text:
A 42-year-old lady with schizophrenia has been tried on Olanzapine and Quetiapine appropriate doses for 8 weeks each with poor e�ect.
Your next step is to try:
questions.explanation:
Kane et al reported a multicenter clinical where schizophrenia patients who had failed to respond to at least three di�erent neuroleptics
underwent a prospective, single-blind trial of rather a high dose of haloperidol for six weeks. Patients whose condition remained
unimproved inspite of haloperidol were then randomly assigned, in a double-blind manner, to clozapine (up to 900 mg/d) or chlorpromazine
(up to 1800 mg/d) for six weeks. Out of 268 patients, 30% of the clozapine-treated patients were categorized as responders compared with
4% of chlorpromazine-treated patients. This improvement included 'negative' as well as positive symptoms.

questions.question_text: The most characteristic symptom of SSRI discontinuation syndrome is
questions.explanation:
The abrupt withdrawal of SSRI especially paroxetine or �uvoxamine (shorter half-life), is associated with dizziness, nausea, headache,
depression, anxiety, insomnia, poor concentration, �u-like symptoms, paresthesias, and migraine-like symptoms. It usually requires at least
6 weeks of treatment before discontinuation and resolves spontaneously in 3 weeks. Those who have signi�cant SSRI intolerance during
treatment onset will have more discontinuation reactions. Fluoxetine is the SSRI least likely to cause withdrawal syndrome as its metabolite
has t1/2 more than 1 week leading to slow self-tapering in plasma. Fluoxetine in some cases can treat discontinuation syndrome or used to
prevent it when stopping an SSRI suddenly. But delayed withdrawal syndrome can occur with �uoxetine too.

questions.question_text: Which of the following may help di�erentiating borderline personality from bipolar disorder?

options.text: Impulsivity in bipolar disorder is chronic rather than episodic
Mood changes lasts for many days in borderline personality
Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality
Borderline personality has a de�nite onset
Elated mood shifts are often seen in borderline personality

correct_answer.text: Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality

questions.explanation:
In Bipolar Disorder the onset is in early 20s (later than borderline), mood changes are observable spontaneoulsy rather than being
precipitated solely by external events, if present, episodic self harm attempts are usually related to depression, though self mutilation is
rare. Patients with borderline PD use 'emptiness' as a descriptor for their mood more often than those with bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text:
A 44-year-old woman repeatedly visits her dentist with numbness around her mouth and pain in the right jaw. There was no observable
�nding on oral and dental examination, and the clinical picture seems inconsistent to the dentist, who refer her to your clinic. The most
likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation:
The term atypical facial pain was �rst introduced by Frazier and Russell in 1924. The pain is atypical in its distribution, unilateral and poorly
localised - not �tting with any cranial neuralgia. It lasts most of the day and is described as a severe ache, crushing or burning sensation. The
Headache Classi�cation Subcommittee of the International Headache Society (2004) described persistent idiopathic facial pain (PIFP) as
Psychiatric symptoms of depression and anxiety are prevalent in this population. Treatment is very di�cult and requires a multidisciplinary
approach to address the many facets of this pain syndrome. Pain disorder is one of several somatoform disorders described in the revised
DSM-IV-TR.

questions.question_text: Psychotic illness in multiple sclerosis is most commonly observed in the context of treatment with
questions.explanation: Exogenous steroids can induce both a�ective disturbances and psychosis.

questions.question_text: 'Giant Panda sign' is an MRI �nding characteristic of
questions.explanation:
Wilson's disease: MRI may show intense hyperintensity of the midbrain with relative sparing of red nucleus, superior colliculus and part of
the pars reticulata of substantia nigra with hypointensity of the aqueduct sometimes called "Giant Panda sign".

questions.question_text: 'Real-life test' forms part of the treatment options for which psychiatric condition?
questions.explanation:
Real-life test forms part of the treatment options for Transsexualism. Most centres require a successful real-life test of at least one year prior
to consideration for surgery. During this time the patient undertakes to live full time and attempt to �nd employment in the new sex.
Patients will change their name and come out to friends and family. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 758

questions.question_text:
A 33-year-old man is suspected to have various sexually transmitted illnesses and possibly HIV. He presents with cognitive impairment.
Which of the following cells in his brain are least likely to be directly a�ected by HIV?
questions.explanation:
Theoretically all the main cell types of the CNS, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, neurons, perivascular macrophage and microglia, can be
infected by HIV-1 since they possess the receptors and/or co-receptors for HIV-1 entry, but only the latter two are the most commonly
infected cells by HIV-1. Most studies have indicated an absence of in vivo infection in neurons - It is unclear whether detection of infected
neurons is complicated by the loss of the infected neuronal populations.

questions.question_text:
A 34-year-old lady presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating but has no weight control behaviour. She has a general tendency to
overeat and looks overweight. Which of the following is correct regarding this presentation?

options.text: Nearly a quarter of those su�ering from this problem are males
Her condition will not remit spontaneously
Stressful periods are associated with decline in binges

correct_answer.text: Nearly a quarter of those su�ering from this problem are males

questions.explanation:
Recurrent episodes of binge eating in the absence of extreme weight-control behaviour generally occurs in a background of a tendency to
overeat. This is referred to as Binge Eating Disorder and is associated with obesity. Patients are typically in their 40s with an
overrepresentation of males when compared to other eating disorderarly 25% of all binge-eating population are males.

questions.question_text:
A 34-year-old patient is started on sertraline by her GP. As a part of local monitoring system the GP administers a depression rating scale
whose minimal score to diagnose depression is 7. The patient's initial score is 22/62. Her score drops to 11/62 in 8 week's time. Which of the
following is true?

options.text: The patient is in partial response

questions.explanation:
Non-response is usually de�ned as 25% or less decrease in symptom severity compared with baseline. Partial response is 26-49% decrease
in symptom severity compared with baseline. Response is 50% or greater decrease in severity of symptoms compared with baseline.
Remission refers to an absence of symptoms de�ned by absolute scale (for example, score of 7 on Hamilton rating scale for depression).

questions.question_text:
A 44-year-old patient has been admitted many times with a relapse of bipolar disorder in last few years. To be classi�ed as a rapid cycler,
which of the following categories must he satisfy?

options.text: More than 4 relapses of either mania or depression in the last year
More than 4 episodes requiring hospitalisation in 1 year
More than 4 episodes of switch in a week
More than 4 manic episodes in last 1 year

correct_answer.text: More than 4 relapses of either mania or depression in the last year

questions.explanation:
The de�nition of rapid cycling is having greater than or equal to 4 episodes/year. This includes both depression and mania. Patients who
have at least 4 episodes/month are considered ultra-rapid cyclers and those who switch within a day on at least 4 days/week are termed
ultra-ultra rapid or ultradian cyclers.

questions.question_text:
A 46-year-old man with schizophrenia is admitted with a history of heavy drinking, poor self-hygiene and self-neglect. He is confused,
agitated and has visual hallucinations. Which of the following is most important to avoid?
questions.explanation:
In patients with alcohol related delirium or cognitive change, start thiamine prior to or concurrently with treatment of intravenous glucose
solutions, and continue until the patient resumes a normal diet. The administration of dextrose or other carbohydrates in this setting can be
hazardous, because glucose oxidation is a thiamine-intensive process that may drive the last reserves of circulating vitamin B-1 toward the
intracellular compartment, thereby aggravating neurologic damage

questions.question_text:
A 46-year-old lady has been treated with Tamoxifen for breast cancer. She is also clinically depressed and will need treatment with
antidepressants. Which one among the following should be avoided due to its e�ects upon Tamoxifen?
questions.explanation:
In several studies (notably, Jin et al, 2005), concurrent use of tamoxifen with the potent CYP2D6-inhibitor antidepressants such as
duloxetine, bupropion, paroxetine and �uoxetine, was associated with a signi�cant reduction in circulating endoxifen levels in some women
and therefore should be avoided.

questions.question_text:
A 50-year-old man with a history of paranoid schizophrenia has been prescribed 600 mg of Quetiapine. During a routine screening with ECG,
he has a QTc interval of 510 ms. He does not report any cardiac symptoms. The appropriate next step would be

options.text: Cross taper quetiapine with Olanzapine and repeat ECG in 2 weeks
Repeat ECG in 2 weeks, since patient is asymptomatic
Repeat ECG and refer to cardiology if T wave is abnormal
Reduce the dose of Quetiapine, repeat ECG and consider referral to cardiology

correct_answer.text: Reduce the dose of Quetiapine, repeat ECG and consider referral to cardiology

questions.explanation:
Strong evidence links QTc values over 500 ms to a clearly increased risk of arrhythmias. The dosage should be reduced immediately and
consider referral to a cardiologist immediately.

questions.question_text: A 54-year-old woman gives a history suggestive of acute anxiety. Which of the following is not consistent with a diagnosis of panic disorder?

options.text: Episodes of unconsciousness in a crowded supermarket
Recurrent experience of pressure symptoms on the chest

correct_answer.text: Episodes of unconsciousness in a crowded supermarket

questions.explanation: Falling 'unconscious' suggests organic cause.

questions.question_text:
A 56-year-old lady treated for bipolar depression wants to know which drug can prevent both mania and depression equally well. The best
option is
questions.explanation:
Bauer et al proposed that an agent be considered a mood stabilizer if it has e�cacy in each of four distinct uses: 1) treatment of acute manic
symptoms, 2) treatment of acute depressive symptoms, 3) prevention of manic symptoms, and 4) prevention of depressive symptoms.
According to their analysis only lithium was eligible to be called a mood stabiliser.

questions.question_text: A Glasgow coma scale between 9-12 indicates which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The GCS is scored between 3 and 15, 3 being the worst, and 15 the best. It is composed of three parameters : Best Eye Response, Best
Verbal Response, Best Motor Response.A Coma Score of 13 or higher correlates with a mild brain injury, 9 to 12 is a moderate injury and 8
or less a severe brain injury. Teasdale G., Jennett B., LANCET (ii) 81-83, 1974.

questions.question_text:
An ST1 trainee in psychiatry sustains a needlestick injury despite wearing gloves. The patient is suspected to have HIV. The risk of HIV
transmission from seropositive individuals following a needlestick injury in health care workers is about
questions.explanation:
The risk of infection of health care workers after a needlestick accident is rare, about 1 in 300. After infection with HIV, AIDS is estimated to
develop in 8 to 11 years, although this time is gradually increasing because of early treatment.

questions.question_text:
A young man in your clinic complains of sti�ness soon after starting antipsychotic treatment. Which of the following scales could most likely

questions.question_text: Focused family interventions are particularly useful in which of the following subgroups with eating disorders?
questions.explanation: Family interventions that directly address the eating disorder are especially useful for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa

questions.question_text: For a patient su�ering from �rst-time relapse of schizophrenia the most e�ective dose of risperidone is
questions.explanation:
For risperidone, a dose of 2 mg daily consistently produced a lower level of e�cacy. Doses of 6 mg or greater produced no additional bene�t
and doses tend to be less e�cacious at 10 mg daily and above. (Ezewuziie and Taylor, 2006). The optimal dose of risperidone in relapsed

questions.question_text: For male to female transsexuals, all of the following surgical procedures are performed except;
questions.explanation:
Surgery for male to female transsexual patients involves Orchidectomy and Penectomy with Vaginoplasty using penile skin. The cosmetic
results can be good, although candidates vary in their ability to be orgasmic post-surgery. For FTM patients' surgery involves bilateral
mastectomy, hysterectomy, and bilateral salpingo-oopherectomy. Phalloplasty is undertaken in less than half of patients as current
techniques are neither cosmetically acceptable nor functional for penetration. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 759

questions.question_text:
Four patients are admitted simultaneously with depression. Mrs A is a 36-year-old woman with 2 previous episodes. Mr B is a 33-year-old
man with a �rst episode. Mrs C has had one previous episode of depression. Mr D, aged 77, has had at least 6 previous episodes. Which of
the following is true?

options.text: Those who do not have recurrence in next 2 years will be free from depression thereafter.
Mr B will have highest recurrence rate.
At least one of them will have a recurrence in next 6 months.
None of the other listed optiions is true
The recurrence rate will be lowest for Mr D given his age.

correct_answer.text: At least one of them will have a recurrence in next 6 months.

questions.explanation:
About 25 percent of patients experience a recurrence of major depressive disorder in the �rst 6 months after release from a hospital, about
30 to 50 percent in the following 2 years, and about 50 to 75 percent in 5 years. Approximately 50% of patients who experience an episode
of major depression will have a recurrence within 5 years. For patients who have had two major depressive episodes, the probability of
recurrence increases to 70%, and after three episodes it increases to 80% to 95%

questions.question_text: Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for which psychiatric condition?
questions.explanation:
Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for Chronic fatigue syndrome. It is based physiological model of
deconditioning. Muscles strength, autonomic response and perception of exercise related sensation are a�ected by inactivity. Therapy aims
to gradually increase the exercise and other activities thus reducing the unwanted consequences of inactivity. CBT and graded exercise
therapy are the only e�ective treatments for CFS.

questions.question_text: In the immediate management of panic disorder which of the following is correct?

options.text: Dose escalation is an optimum strategy for SSRIs
Combination of CBT and SSRIs must be tried whenever possible
Benzodiazepines must be given for all those waiting for CBT
Psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy have comparable e�cacy

correct_answer.text: Psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy have comparable e�cacy

questions.explanation:
acute management according to patient choice: pharmacological: all SSRIs, some TCAs (clomipramine, imipramine), some benzodiazepines
(alprazolam, clonazepam, diazepam, lorazepam), venlafaxine, reboxetine have evidence base. psychological: cognitive-behaviour therapy
Both pharmacological and psychological approaches have broadly similar e�cacy in acute treatment. Routinely combining drug and
psychological approaches is not recommended

questions.question_text:
Both CBT and mentalization-based therapy have a positive e�ect in treating depression. A randomised, parallel group, assessor-blinded
superiority clinical trial is planned to compare the two approaches. 84 consecutive adult participants diagnosed with major depressive
disorder and receiving antidepressant treatment, (unchanged for the last 6 weeks) will be included over the course of 2 years, randomised
to either CBT or mentalization-based therapy. The primary outcome is a change in the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression at cessation of
treatment (18 weeks). The investigators intend to use an Intention to Treat Analysis (ITT) when reporting the study results. Excluding which
of the following subjects will not a�ect the principle of ITT analysis?

options.text: Patients in Mentalization arm who disclose receiving private CBT sessions
Patients who disclose a new private prescription of �uoxetine during the trial
Patients who withdraw their consent after completing the trial
Patients who are allocated to CBT halfway after incorrectly receiving treatment in the Mentalization arm.

correct_answer.text: Patients who are allocated to CBT halfway after incorrectly receiving treatment in the Mentalization arm.

questions.explanation:
Intention to treat approach maintains treatment groups that are similar, apart from random variation. This is the reason for randomisation,
and the feature may be lost if the analysis is not performed on the groups produced by the randomisation process. For this reason,
dropouts due to death or consent-withdrawal must not be excluded (Note: ethical permission must be sought beforehand to use the data
from patients who discontinue the trial). Certain protocol-deviations may also happen in real world practice: e.g. self-medicating patients or
those who do not take the treatment as prescribed. These exceptions must not induce exclusion of patients in an ITT analysis. Excluding
randomised patients from the primary analysis may be legitimate when study personnel made errors in the implementation of eligibility
criteria or when patients did not receive the correct intervention – an error that can happen only in a trial set-up. Ref: Fergusson et al BMJ.
2002; 325(7365): 652 –654 & Hollis & Campbell, BMJ 1999;319:670

questions.question_text:

placebo — and followed monthly for up to 36 months. Of the enrolled 4758 couples 4747 were followed: 1584 randomly assigned to TDF,
1579 to TDF –FTC, and 1584 to placebo. A total of 82 HIV-1 infections occurred in seronegative participants during the study, 17 in the TDF
group, 13 in the TDF –FTC group and 52 in the placebo group, indicating a relative reduction of 67% in the incidence of HIV-1 with TDF (95%
con�dence interval [CI], 44 to 81; P<0.001) and of 75% with TDF –FTC (95% CI, 55 to 87; P<0.001). Protective e�ects of TDF –FTC and TDF
alone against HIV-1 were not signi�cantly di�erent (P=0.23), and both study medications signi�cantly reduced the HIV-1 incidence among
both men and women. Eight participants receiving active treatment were found to have been infected with HIV-1 at baseline, and among
these, antiretroviral resistance developed in two during the study. An estimate of the primary endpoint in the modi�ed Intention-to-Treat
Analysis is shown in a graph below. The primary endpoint of this study is

options.text: Antiretroviral treatment response in seropositive partners
Emergence of immunity against HIV-1 infection

questions.explanation:
This study evaluated the ability of antiretroviral treatment to prevent HIV-1 infection in individuals who have seropositive partners. The
preexposure prophylaxis was provided to originally seronegative partners.

questions.question_text:
As a specialty doctor in an addiction clinic, you are concerned that the increase in the rate of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) in your
area may be linked to high rates of methamphetamine use locally. You conduct a qualitative study initially by interviewing several patients
and devise an educational intervention (FATA: Focussed Addiction Therapist Advice). To test the e�ectiveness of this intervention, you
decided to provide FATA to alternate patients attending your clinic. Using this information answer the following question. To test your hunch
that FATA is an e�ective intervention, what study design have you used in the above scenario?
questions.explanation:
You are testing an intervention – i.e. conducting a trial. You have some 'controls' for whom the active treatment is not being o�ered (i.e. your
alternate patients who don't receive FATA). So you are running a controlled trial. You haven't randomised this sample, so this is a simple
controlled trial, but not randomised. Note that the non-randomised controlled trials can detect associations between an intervention and an
outcome, though they cannot rule out the possibility that the association was confounded.

questions.question_text:
As a specialty doctor in an addiction clinic, you are concerned that the increase in the rate of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) in your
area may be linked to high rates of methamphetamine use locally. You conduct a qualitative study initially by interviewing several patients
and devise an educational intervention (FATA: Focussed Addiction Therapist Advice). To test the e�ectiveness of this intervention, you
decided to provide FATA to alternate patients attending your clinic. Using this information answer the following question. For the qualitative
study described above, what is the best method of data collection?
questions.explanation:
Focus groups are a form of group interview that capitalises on communication between research participants in order to generate data.
Although group interviews are often used simply as a quick and convenient way to collect data from several people simultaneously, focus
groups explicitly use group interaction as part of the method. BMJ 1995;311:299

questions.question_text:
As a specialty doctor in an addiction clinic, you are concerned that the increase in the rate of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) in your
area may be linked to high rates of methamphetamine use locally. You conduct a qualitative study initially by interviewing several patients
and devise an educational intervention (FATA: Focussed Addiction Therapist Advice). To test the e�ectiveness of this intervention, you
decided to provide FATA to alternate patients attending your clinic. Using this information answer the following question. What is the
primary outcome of the study that investigates the e�ect of the educational intervention?

options.text: The degree of patients' understanding of methamphetamine and STDs relationship

questions.explanation:
The primary concern seems to be the incidence of STDs. The educational intervention, by reducing risky sexual habits in methamphetamine
users, aims to reduce this incidence. An increase in patients' understanding of the relationship is a proxy endpoint.

questions.question_text:
As a specialty doctor in an addiction clinic, you are concerned that the increase in the rate of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) in your
area may be linked to high rates of methamphetamine use locally. You conduct a qualitative study initially by interviewing several patients
and devise an educational intervention (FATA: Focussed Addiction Therapist Advice). To test the e�ectiveness of this intervention, you
decided to provide FATA to alternate patients attending your clinic. Using this information answer the following question. What is the most
appropriate study design to investigate the relationship between methamphetamine use and the rate of STDs?
questions.explanation:
To investigate the association between two phenomena, an observational study measuring incidence rates of the co-occurrence both
problems (i.e. STDs and methamphetamine use) is a good starting point. To establish causality, this won't be su�cient, a cohort study may
be more appropriate.

questions.explanation: SEM is given by SD/sqrt.N = 18/sqrt.81 = 18/9 = 2.

questions.question_text: For healthcare interventions not restricted to a speci�c specialty, which database is commonly used to identify observational studies?
questions.explanation:

options.text: Selecting subjects who are uniform for confounding variables

The best method is to avoid confounders by sampling in a matched fashion. But one may not be able to avoid unknown confounders in this

If the pooled estimate is given in odds ratio, then the midline of a forest plot which represents 'a line of no e�ect' corresponds to a value of

questions.question_text: If the sensitivity of a test increases which of the following occurs?

options.text: The power of statistical test drops.
The false positive error rate increases.
The false negative error rate increases.

correct_answer.text: The false positive error rate increases.

questions.explanation:
When sensitivity increases, more number of cases will be diagnosed despite not having the disease (an increase in false positive rate). When
you select a lower criterion value, then the true positive fraction and sensitivity will increase. On the other hand, the false positive fraction
will also increase, and, therefore, the true negative fraction and speci�city will decrease.

questions.question_text: In a forest plot, what does the horizontal line passing through the block depict?
questions.explanation:
In a forest plot, the horizontal line passing through the block depicts the con�dence interval. In other words, the lines running across the
'OR' (Odds ratio) dot represents the con�dence interval for that odds ratio.

questions.question_text:
In a sample of 300 volunteers, IQ is measured and the value is plotted as a distribution curve across the sample. It is found that the mean,
median, and mode are all the same for the sample studied. Which of the following statistical distribution refers to the above pattern?
questions.explanation:
One of the characteristic features of Normal or Gaussian distribution is that the mean, median and mode of the observations lie at the same
point. A bimodal distribution has 2 mode values. In a negatively skewed distribution, the mean is lesser than the median. The tail of such a
distribution is longer on the left than the right (negative outliers). In a positively skewed distribution, the mean is greater than the median.
The tail of such a distribution is longer on the right than the left (positive outliers).

questions.question_text:
In a scale designed to measure the creativity of a population, it was found that the scores obtained were normally distributed. If mean score
is 10 and standard deviation is 1, then the proportion of population who will score between 9 and 11 is
questions.explanation:
The value 9 is nothing but (mean – 1SD) while 11 is (mean + 1SD). Between -1 and +1SD we can expect to see 68% observations in a normal
distribution.

questions.question_text: In a study comparing two treatments for depression, which of the following is associated with greater statistical power?

options.text: Comparison of active drug against active drug
The use of a categorical outcome variable
Comparison of active drug against placebo

correct_answer.text: Comparison of active drug against placebo

questions.explanation:
When two active compounds are compared, the observed size of the e�ect tends to be smaller for a given sample size. But when a placebo
is compared against an active drug, the power of a study increases.

As a �rst step, calculate Standard error from SD and total N (sample size). SE = SD / sqRt of N = 15/6 = 2.5. To get 95% con�dence values, add

correct_answer.text: The more the unemployed days, the more the functional impairment

questions.explanation: 0.81 is a signi�cant positive correlation

questions.question_text:
In a systematic review of studies looking at Duration of Untreated Psychosis and outcome, two types of study designs are noted. One group
of studies categorically divided DUP to binary variable long DUP and short DUP and assessed the outcome. Another group of studies
correlated the duration of DUP with the severity of the outcome. Which of the following best describes the above phenomenon?
questions.explanation:
In systematic reviews, heterogeneity refers to variability or di�erences between studies in the estimates of e�ects. A distinction should
made between "statistical heterogeneity" (di�erences in the reported e�ects), "methodological heterogeneity" (di�erences in study design)
and "clinical heterogeneity" (di�erences between studies in key characteristics of the participants, interventions or outcome measures). In
this question, the study methods are di�erent – as a result methodological heterogeneity has resulted. (from Bandolier)

questions.question_text: The absolute di�erence between two treatments in a study is 10% (95% C.I; 5% to 15%). What is the 95% C.I for the NNT.
questions.explanation:
95% C.I for NNT is calculated by using the 95% C.I values of the ABI (Absolute di�erence). The NNT for the ABI of 5 is 1/0.05=20. The NNT for
the ABI of 15 is 1/0.15=6.6, corrected to 7. So, the C. I for the NNT is 7 to 20.

questions.question_text: The age and sex structure of a population are best illustrated as a
questions.explanation:
A population pyramid also called an age structure programme, is a graphical illustration that shows the distribution of various age groups in
a human population which normally forms the shape of a pyramid. It is often viewed as the most e�ective way to graphically depict the age

questions.question_text: The expression obtained by square root of variance is called
questions.explanation:
Standard deviation is the square root of the variance. The standard error is a measure obtained by the ratio of standard deviation of mean
to the square root of sample size.

The study with the maximum number of subjects
The study with the most precise result

questions.question_text: The medical database where you can obtain abstracts published since 1890 is
questions.explanation: PsycINFO has the records from 1890; Medline has items from 1949 (few classical older papers may be occasionally found)

questions.question_text: The medical database where you can obtain papers related to nursing and allied health disciplines is
questions.explanation:
CINAHL (Cumulative Index of Nursing and Allied Health) indexes journals in the �elds of nursing and allied health from 1982. PsycINFO is an
abstract database of psychological literature from the 1800s to the present. EMBASE (Excerpta Medica database) is a biomedical database
that contains bibliographic records with citations, abstracts and indexing derived from biomedical articles in peer-reviewed journals, and is
especially strong in its coverage of drug and pharmaceutical research from 1974. MEDLINE (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System

questions.question_text: The most conservative way of dealing with missing data in intention to treat analysis is
questions.explanation:
In the worst case scenario analysis, all missing data is treated as non-responders for the intervention group and responders for a control
group (the worst possible case for the researcher). This is the most conservative of all methods to �ll missing data.

questions.question_text: The most frequently combined studies in meta-analyses are
questions.explanation: RCTs are the most frequently combined studies for a meta-analysis though it is possible to combine other study designs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following bias is controlled by allocation concealment?
questions.explanation: Allocation concealment helps to reduce selection bias while blinding helps to reduce ascertainment bias.

questions.question_text: Which of the following clinical questions is better suited to qualitative rather than quantitative research methods?

options.text: A study to measure psychiatric symptoms after head injury
A study detailing the functional outcomes of people treated with Cognitive Behavioural Therapy

questions.explanation:
Qualitative research is often employed to understand the feelings, values, and perceptions that underlie and in�uence behaviour/health
states.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions must be satis�ed for odds ratio to come close or be the same as a relative risk?

questions.question_text: Which of the following data can provide a link between exposure to a risk factor and the disease studied?
questions.explanation:
Incidence rates are useful in epidemiological research for causality. Incidence rates can provide data on new cases developing after an
exposure within a time period in a speci�ed population. Thus they are more useful than prevalence data to obtain a link between exposure
and disease development.

questions.emi_instruction: For each of the descriptions below choose one appropriate proposal or guideline regulating the report or conduct of research studies
questions.question_text:
Proposal to improve the reporting of observational studies in the
�eld of epidemiology
questions.explanation:
PRISMA - Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses - is an evidence-based minimum set of items for
reporting in systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Though the main focus is on RCTs, PRISMA can also be used as a basis for reporting
systematic reviews of other types of research. Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) group suggested a proposal
for reporting a meta-analysis of observational studies in epidemiology ('MOOSE'). STROBE stands for an international, collaborative initiative
of epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors involved in the conduct and dissemination of observational
studies, with the common aim of STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology. The ASSERT statement is the
articulation of A Standard for the Scienti�c and Ethical Review of Trials. It proposes a structured approach whereby research ethics
committees review proposals for and monitor the conduct of, randomized controlled clinical trials. CONSORT statement is an evidence-
based, minimum set of recommendations for reporting RCTs. QUOROM statement is an evidence-based minimum set of recommendations
for improving the quality of reporting of meta-analyses of clinical randomised controlled trials (RCTs).
